# Adapting the book for your course {#adapting}

The book is meant to be changed. Each chapter is a separate R Markdown file,
each example starts from one data chunk, and the book builds with one
command, so you can reorder chapters, replace examples with your own data,
or add a chapter for a topic you teach.

## The files {-}

All sources are in the
[`book/` folder](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse/tree/main/book) of
the mirtverse repository:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `index.Rmd` | Title page and preface |
| `00-author.Rmd` | About the author |
| `01-measurement.Rmd` to `12-reporting.Rmd` | The twelve chapters, one per course week |
| `13-ml-lens.Rmd`, `14-item-text.Rmd`, `15-aig.Rmd`, `16-auto-scoring.Rmd`, `17-llms.Rmd`, `18-ai-validity.Rmd` | The chapters on AI in measurement |
| `90-datasets.Rmd`, `91-adapting.Rmd` | The appendices |
| `_bookdown.yml` | Chapter order (`rmd_files`) and output folder |
| `_output.yml` | Look of the HTML, PDF and EPUB editions |
| `latex/` | Title page, preamble and box styles of the PDF edition |
| `cover/` | Cover artwork and how to regenerate it |
| `_common.R` | Code run before every chapter: Loads mirtverse and sets chunk options |
| `references.bib` | References cited in the book |

Table: (\#tab:files) Source files of the book.

The chapter files and their ids (`{#measurement}`, `{#irt-models}` and so
on) are kept stable, so links to a chapter keep working across versions.

## Every chapter has the same shape {-}

1. A **Learning goals** box.
2. **Key terms**, linked to the glossary.
3. **The ideas.**
4. **Example 1** and **Example 2**, each starting with a data chunk labelled
   `data-<chapter id>-1` or `-2`.
5. **Your turn**, with solutions in a folded `<details>` block.
6. **In the lab** and **Further reading**.

Keep this shape when you add a chapter, and students will always know where
to look.

## Swapping in your own data {-}

To use your own data in an example, replace the body of its data chunk and
keep the label and the object names listed in Appendix \@ref(datasets). For
example, to run Example 1 of Chapter \@ref(irt-models) on your own
dichotomous test:

````markdown
```{r data-irt-models-1}`r ''`
# Our midterm: 40 multiple-choice items, scored 0/1.
resp <- read.csv("midterm-scored.csv")[, -1]   # drop the ID column
```
````

The rest of the example then runs on your data. Two caveats:

* Examples built on **simulated** data compare estimates with the true
  values used to simulate them (objects such as `true`, `true_theta` or the
  planted DIF items). With real data there is no truth, so delete those
  comparisons or turn them into questions for students.
* The prose describes the original results. Re-read the text around each
  output after you swap the data, and edit the interpretation to match.

The mirtverse instructor toolkit automates these steps, for example copying
a chapter into a course folder and replacing a data chunk; see the
[instructor toolkit
guide](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/instructor-toolkit.html).

## Building the book {-}

Install bookdown once, then build from the `book/` folder:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("bookdown")
bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd")           # the whole book, into _book/
bookdown::preview_chapter("05-fit.Rmd")      # one chapter, faster
```

Open `_book/index.html` in a browser to read the result. The whole book
builds in a few minutes on a laptop. To publish your own version, put the
`_book/` folder on any web server, or use GitHub Pages as the mirtverse
repository does (its `book` workflow builds the book and publishes it next
to the package website).

## Suggesting changes {-}

Every page has a *Suggest an edit* link at the top, which opens the
chapter's source on GitHub. Corrections and new examples are welcome as
issues or pull requests in the [mirtverse
repository](https://github.com/okanbulut/mirtverse).
